### iliad-095 (15.377–470)

| Greek | English (`l` / `i`) | reason |
|---|---|---|
| Αἴας δ’ ἐρρίγησε, κασίγνητον δὲ προσηύδα (15.436, whole-line speech introduction; 15.466 with Τεῦκρος) | "And Ajax shuddered, and his brother he addressed:" / "Ajax shuddered, and spoke to his brother:" (466: "And Teucer shuddered, and his brother he addressed:" / "Teucer shuddered, and spoke to his brother:") | ῥιγέω keeps "shudder" (the table's ῥίγησεν, 3.259, 15.34); κασίγνητος "brother"; προσηύδα "addressed" in `l`, "spoke to" in `i`, as the table's προσηύδα rows; avoided: "shivered", "was seized with fear" (the Greek names no cause) |
| ἰοδόκον (φαρέτρην, 15.444; ἰός "arrow" + the root of δέχομαι) | "arrow-receiving" / "arrow-holding" | avoided: "arrow-bearing", "full of arrows"; φαρέτρη keeps "quiver" (10.260), ἰός "arrow" |
| ὠκύμοροι (ἰοί, 15.440; of arrows, active sense) | "swift-doomed" / "that bring swift doom" | a departure from the table's passive sense for persons (ὠκύμορος "swift to your doom", 1.417; the Odyssey's ὠκύμοροι "meet a swift doom"): the root keeps "swift … doom", but arrows do not meet their doom, they bring it, and the note says so; avoided: "short-lived", "swift-fated" |
| πολύστονος (ἰός, 15.451; of an arrow) | "much-groaning" / "of the many groans" (+ note: "causing many groans") | follows the table's πολύστονος "much-groaning" / "of many groans" (11.73) |
| χαλκοβαρής (ἰός, 15.465; χαλκός + βαρύς) | "bronze-heavy" / "bronze-heavy" | avoided: "heavy-headed", "bronze-weighted", "heavy with bronze" |
| ναύμαχα κολλήεντα (ξυστοῖσι, 15.389) | "ship-fighting, glued" / "made for fighting at sea, glued together" | ναύμαχος "ship-fighting" (ναῦς + μάχομαι), κολλήεις "glued" (κόλλα); ξυστόν keeps "polished spear" (11.565); avoided: "for sea-battle", "jointed", "fitted" |
| ἀγαπήνορος Εὐρυπύλοιο (15.392) | "man-cherishing Eurypylus" / "Eurypylus, who prized manliness" | follows the table's ἀγαπήνωρ (13.756, with the note that the sense is not known) |
| νεῖκος (μέγα νεῖκος ὄρωρεν, 15.400; = 12.122 δὴ γὰρ μέγα νεῖκος ὄρωρεν, iliad-078) | "for now a great quarrel has arisen" / "for a great quarrel has now arisen" (+ note: the fighting itself) | νεῖκος keeps "quarrel" (the table, 1.319, 2.376) and the line keeps the English it has at 12.122; avoided: "strife" (ἔρις), "conflict", "has broken out" |
| ἐξείλετο θυμόν (15.460; ἐξαιρέω middle) | "had taken out his life" / "taken his life" | θυμός of the life that leaves the body is "life" (the table's θυμὸν ἐξαίνυτο, 5.155); avoided: "heart", "spirit" |
| Διὸς πυκινὸν νόον (15.461) | "the close-packed mind of Zeus" / "the shrewd mind of Zeus" | follows the table's πυκινὴν βουλήν "close-packed plan" / "shrewd plan" (2.55) |
| Τεῦκρον Τελαμώνιον εὖχος ἀπηύρα (15.462) | "from Telamonian Teucer took away the boast" / "robbed Telamonian Teucer of his triumph" | εὖχος "boast" in `l`, "triumph" in `i` (the table, 5.285, 22.7); ἀπαυράω "take away" with two accusatives; Τελαμώνιος "Telamonian", as for Ajax |
| σὺν δαίμονι (15.403) · δαίμων (15.418, 15.468) | "with some power" · "a power" / "with some power’s help" · "some power" | σὺν δαίμονι as in the table (11.792) and δαίμων as in the Odyssey table (6.172) and 11.480, for one unnamed god acting on a man; "divinity" of the Iliad table (1.222, 3.420) is for a being, not an acting power |
